title: Medical reimbursement stalled for months, tribal patients of Ranni left in the lurch
content: Vulnerable patients from the Scheduled Tribe (ST) communities in Ranni, Pathanamthitta, are facing immense hardships as the reimbursement of their medicine bills has been stalled for over four months. Despite submitting all necessary documents to the ST Development Department, many patients have not received a single rupee, forcing them to borrow money or skip life-saving medications. Under the existing welfare scheme, tribal patients suffering from chronic illnesses such as diabetes, heart disease, and kidney failure (including those undergoing dialysis or bypass surgery) are entitled to buy medicines from private medical stores if they are unavailable at government hospitals. The expenses are supposed to be reimbursed upon submitting the bills to the local ST Welfare Office. However, bureaucratic red tape and technical glitches have brought this crucial support system to a grinding halt. Technical glitch halts payments The reimbursement bills are processed through the local Tribal Extension Officer and the District Welfare Officer before being forwarded to the Directorate for final approval. According to local officials, the prolonged delay is primarily due to technical glitches within the department's web portal, which has failed to process the applications. While the authorities point to digital errors, patients who depend on these monthly payouts for their survival are left to suffer. The crisis is further compounded by the prolonged absence of key administrative figures in Ranni, including the District Tribal Officer and the Tribal Extension Officer. This administrative vacuum has severely disrupted welfare and relief operations in tribal settlements, which are especially crucial during the monsoon season when waterborne diseases and physical isolation pose severe threats to these communities.
